title: Ethiopian Physics University Entrance Exam 2014
description: Ethiopian Physics University Entrance Exam 2014 featuring 100 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: Suppose a triangular object (O) is placed in front of a plane mirror and its image is formed at position (I). Which one of the following diagrams represents the image (I) formed by the mirror when it is observed from position (X)?
questions.explanation:
A plane mirror forms a virtual image that is the same size as the object, located the same distance behind the mirror, and is laterally inverted (left and right reversed).

 Diagram D correctly shows the image (I) as a lateral reversal of the object (O) at an equal distance from the mirror.

questions.questionText: An object is placed 25.0 cm in front of a concave mirror having focal length of 10.0 cm. The magnification of the mirror is _________.
questions.explanation:
The image distance (v) is found using the mirror formula: 1/v = 1/f - 1/u. 

With f = -10.0 cm and u = -25.0 cm, 1/v = 1/(-10) - 1/(-25) = -1/10 + 1/25 = (-5 + 2)/50 = -3/50, so v = -50/3 cm.

 The magnification (M) is then M = -v/u = -(-50/3) / (-25) = -2/3 = -0.67. 

The magnitude is 0.67, which corresponds to option C.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements distinguishes between random and systematic errors?
options: Systematic error can be minimized by taking several readings and averaging; whereas random error cannot be minimized.
Systematic error makes measured values to be always above or always below the true value; whereas random error causes measured values to be sometimes above and sometimes below the true value.
Random error makes measured values to be always above or always below the true value; whereas systematic error causes measured values to be sometimes above and sometimes below the true value.
Random error is biased, whereas systematic error does not show bias.
questions.explanation:
Systematic errors introduce a consistent bias, always shifting measurements in the same direction.

 Random errors cause unpredictable scattering of measurements around the true value, being sometimes above and sometimes below.

questions.questionText: The unit vector in the direction of A = 3i+4j is ______.
questions.explanation:
"The unit vector in the direction of a vector A is given by u = A / |A|.

 Here, |A| = √(3² + 4²) = 5.

 Therefore, u = (3i + 4j) / 5 = 3i/5 + 4j/5.

questions.questionText: Which of the following pair of vectors are collinear?
questions.explanation:
Two vectors are collinear if one is a scalar multiple of the other.

 Here, -2 × (2i + 3j) = -4i - 6j, so these vectors are collinear.

questions.questionText: For an object moving in straight line, ______.
options: the displacement changes by equal amount in equal time interval, if the displacement-time graph is horizontal line.
the area of the region under the displacement-time graph and the slope of velocity-time graph are, respectively, the acceleration and displacement of the object.
if the velocity increases by equal amount in equal time interval, the velocity-time graph is straight line with positive slope and the acceleration-time graph is horizontal.
the slope of displacement-time graph and the area of the region under acceleration-time graph are, respectively, the acceleration and velocity of the object.
questions.explanation:
If velocity increases by equal amounts in equal time intervals, the object has constant positive acceleration (a > 0). 

This means the **velocity-time graph must be a straight line with a positive slope. 

For constant acceleration, the acceleration-time graph is a horizontal line (since acceleration isn't changing).

 This is the definition of uniformly accelerated motion.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about satellite motion?
options: satellite moving closer to the Earth takes longer time to complete one revolution than a satellite farther from the Earth.
For two satellites moving around the Earth at equal orbital radius, a heavier satellite has larger speed than a lighter one.
For equal orbital radius, a satellite moving around the Earth has smaller speed than a satellite moving about Moon.
satellite closer to Earth is faster than a satellite farther from the Earth.
questions.explanation:
According to orbital mechanics, the orbital speed of a satellite is given by:- 

v = √(GM/r), where r is the distance from the center of the Earth.

 Therefore, a satellite closer to Earth (smaller r) moves faster than one farther away.

questions.questionText:
A block of mass m is placed on horizontal surface. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the surface is μ. A force of magnitude F acts on the block at an angle θ as shown in the figure below.

The minimum magnitude of the force F required to slide the block on the surface is _______.
questions.explanation:
Resolve the applied force F into components: horizontal = Fcosθ, vertical = Fsinθ (downward).

 The normal force becomes N = mg + Fsinθ.

- Maximum static friction = μN = μ(mg + Fsinθ).

 At the point of motion: Fcosθ = μ(mg + Fsinθ).

 Rearranging gives F(cosθ − μsinθ) = 
μmg, so F = μmg / (cosθ − μsinθ).

questions.questionText: A ball of mass m moving with a speed v strikes a hard wall at an angle θ with the wall. It is reflected with the same speed at the same angle as shown in the figure below. If the ball is in contact with the wall for time t, then the average force acting on the wall is given by _______.
questions.explanation:
Only the velocity component perpendicular to the wall changes.

 Initial normal component = mvcosθ toward wall, final = mvcosθ away from wall.

 Change in momentum = 2mvcosθ.

 Average force = change in momentum / time = (2mvcosθ) / t..

questions.questionText: According to the work-energy theorem, ______.
options: work done by tension on an object tied to a string and moving in a horizontal circle is negative.
work done by gravity on an object thrown downward is negative.
work done by gravity on an object thrown upward and moving upward is negative.
work done by gravitational force on a satellite moving around the earth in a circular orbit is positive.
questions.explanation:
The work-energy theorem states that the work done by forces on an object equals the change in its kinetic energy.

 When an object is thrown upward, gravity acts downward opposite to the motion, so the work done by gravity is negative.

questions.questionText: Standing wave is formed when two identical waves travelling in opposite directions in the same medium interfere with each other. If y1 and y2 are the interfering waves and y = y1 + y2 is the resulting standing wave, which of the following is a correct combination?
options: y1 = Asin(kx - ωt), y2 = Asin(kx +  ωt), y = Asin(kx)cos(2ωt)
y1 = Asin(kx - ωt), y2 = Asin(kx +  ωt), y = 2Asin(kx)cos(ωt)
y1 = Asin(kx - ωt), y2 = Asin(kx -  ωt), y = 2Asin(kx)sin(ωt)
y1 = Asin(kx - ωt), y2 = Acos(kx +  ωt), y = 2Asin(kx -ωt)
questions.explanation:
{Two identical waves traveling in opposite directions are y1 = Asin(kx − ωt) and y2 = Asin(kx + ωt).

 Adding them using sinA + sinB = 2sin((A+B)/2)cos((A−B)/2) gives y = 2Asin(kx)cos(ωt), which matches option 2.}

questions.questionText: A Young double slit experiment consists of two narrow slits separated by 0.06 mm and 1.2m away from a screen. If the slits are illuminated with a light of wavelength 563 nm, the location of the fourth bright fringe on the screen is ______.
questions.explanation:
Use y = nλD/d.
 Substituting n = 4, λ = 563 nm, D = 1.2 m, and d = 0.06 mm gives 

y = 0.045 m = 4.5 cm."
}

questions.questionText: An electric dipole consists of a negative charge -q placed at a point with x and y coordinates (-2, -2) and a positive charge +q at (2, 2). The dipole is placed in a uniform electric field E directed in the positive x direction. If the dipole axis makes an angle θ with the field, which of the following is true about the dipole?
options: The field rotates the dipole in the direction of decreasing the angle θ, until the dipole becomes parallel to the field.
The field rotates it in the direction of increasing the angle θ, until the dipole is perpendicular to the field.
It is in both translational and rotational equilibrium.
It travels in the direction of the electric field.
questions.explanation:
A dipole in a uniform electric field experiences a torque τ = p × E, where p is the dipole moment.

 The torque acts to rotate the dipole such that the dipole moment aligns with the field (θ decreases).

 Once parallel, the torque becomes zero.

questions.questionText: The electric potential at a distance of 2cm from a -1.6 * 10⁻⁹ C point charge is ______.
questions.explanation:
The electric potential due to a point charge is given by V = kQ / r,

 where k = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C², Q = -1.6 × 10⁻⁹ C, and r = 0.02 m.

V = (9 × 10⁹ × -1.6 × 10⁻⁹) / 0.02 = -720 V.

Since the charge is negative, the potential is also negative.

questions.questionText: Two resistors R1 = 1Ω and R2 = 4Ω are connected in parallel to each other and their combination is connected in series with a third resistor R3 = 2Ω. The whole combination is connected to a voltage source of Potential difference 14V. The potential difference across R1 is ______.
questions.explanation:
First, find the equivalent resistance of R1 and R2 in parallel:

 1/Rp = 1/1 + 1/4 = 5/4,

 so Rp = 4/5 = 0.8 Ω.
 Then add R3 in series: Rtotal = 0.8 + 2 = 2.8 Ω.

 Next, calculate total current: I = V/R = 14 / 2.8 = 5 A.

 The voltage across the parallel combination is Vp = I × Rp = 5 × 0.8 = 4 V.

 Since R1 is in parallel with R2, the voltage across R1 is the same as Vp, which is 4 V.

questions.questionText: Consider a long and tightly wound solenoid carrying current I, having length L and N turns of winding. If n is the number of turns per unit length, which of the following describes the magnetic field produced by the solenoid?
options: The magnetic field inside the solenoid is zero, whereas the field outside is perpendicular to the length of the solenoid.
The magnetic field inside the solenoid is constant and is parallel to the solenoid's axis, whereas the field outside is negligible.
The magnetic field inside the solenoid is uniform and perpendicular to the axis of the solenoid.
The magnetic field outside the solenoid is as strong as the field inside it.
questions.explanation:
For a long solenoid, the magnetic field inside is uniform, strong, and parallel to the solenoid's axis, given by B = μ₀ n I, where n = N/L.

 The field outside is very weak and often considered negligible.

questions.questionText: According to the law of electromagnetic induction, ______.
options: the magnitude of emf induced in a circuit is directly proportional to the rate of change the magnetic flux crossing any surface bounded by the circuit.
changing magnetic field parallel to the plane of a circuit induces an emf in it.
constant magnetic flux crossing the surface of a circuit induced an emf in the circuit.
an emf is induced in a circuit when a constant magnetic field crosses its surface.
questions.explanation:
Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction states that the induced emf in a closed circuit is equal to the negative rate of change of magnetic flux through the circuit: emf = -dΦB/dt.

 Only a changing magnetic flux produces an emf.

questions.questionText: A resistor R, a capacitor C, and an inductor L are connected in series to an AC voltage source that generates a sinusoidal voltage V(t) = Vpsin(Ωt), with Vp and Ω being the peak voltage and angular frequency of the source. If XL, XC, and Z are capacitive reactance, inductive reactance, and impedance, respectively, Irms and Vrms are the root-mean-square (rms) values of the current and voltage, the average power dissipated in series RLC circuit is given by ______.
questions.explanation:
Only the resistor dissipates power.

 Average power P = Irms × Vrms × cosφ, and 

cosφ = R/Z = R/√(R² + (XL − XC)²).

 So, P = Irms × Vrms × R/√(R² + (XL − XC)²).

questions.questionText: According to the Heisenberg's uncertainty principle,
options: the faster the position uncertainty, the larger the momentum uncertainty.
if the uncertainty in position decreases, the momentum uncertainty decreases, too.
the more precisely we measure the position of a particle; we become less precise of its momentum and vice versa.
we can measure both the position and momentum of a particle simultaneously with unlimited precision.
questions.explanation:
Heisenberg's uncertainty principle states that the product of the uncertainties in position (Δx) and momentum (Δp) of a particle satisfies Δx·Δp ≥ ħ/2.

 Therefore, increasing precision in measuring position increases the uncertainty in momentum, and vice versa

questions.questionText: The graph of nuclear binding energy per nucleon(BE/A) versus mass number (A) has its peak near an atomic weight A = 56. Which of the following statements is true about the graph?
options: Uranium (A = 235), which has larger binding energy than iron (A=56), is more stable than iron.
Nucleus with larger number of neutron is more stable than nucleus of the same atom with smaller number of neutron.
For heavier nuclei (A > 56), the binding energy per nucleon decreases with the increase of mass number; implying that heavier atoms can increase their stability by increasing their protons' number.
For smaller atoms (A < 56), the binding energy per nucleon generally increases with the increase of mass number; indicating that lighter atoms can increase stability through *nuclear fission*.
questions.explanation:
The binding energy per nucleon graph peaks around iron (A ≈ 56).

 Lighter nuclei (A < 56) have lower binding energy per nucleon and can release energy through nuclear fusion, while heavier nuclei (A > 56) can release energy through fission.

 Iron and nearby nuclei are the most stable

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about reflection and refraction of sound waves and their applications?
options: In pre-natal scanning, reflection and refraction of sound allows doctors to monitor the progress of a developing baby.
Reflection of sound (echo) is formed when sound enters a medium of varying density.
Reflection and refraction of sound are used to detect flaws in metals and to help people park their cars.
Refraction of sound is the change in its direction as it travels through a medium having different densities.
questions.explanation:
An echo is formed due to the reflection of sound from a surface, not when it enters a medium of different density.

 Refraction involves bending due to changing medium, whereas reflection involves bouncing off a surface.

questions.questionText: A torque τ rotates an object of mass m and moment of inertia I through an angle θ. The work done on the object by the torque is ______.
questions.explanation:
The work done by a torque τ when it rotates an object through an angle θ (in radians) is given by W = τ × θ.
]n This is analogous to linear work W = F × d, but for rotational motion.

questions.questionText: A satellite revolves around the Earth in a circular orbit of radius r = 4 * 10¹⁶m. The period of the satellite is ______.
questions.explanation:
The period T of a satellite in a circular orbit is given by:- 

T = 2π√(r³ / GM), 
where G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg² and M = 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg (mass of Earth).

 Substituting r = 4 × 10¹⁶ m gives T ≈ 2.5 × 10¹⁹ s.

questions.questionText: One of the following statements is a correct description of the charging processes?
options: During charging a neutral object by induction using a negatively charged rod, charge flows from the rod to the object.
When a neutral metallic sphere is charged by induction using a negatively charged rod, the sphere acquires a net negative charge.
When a positively charged object is momentarily brought into contact with a neutral metallic sphere, the sphere acquires a net positive charge.
When a plastic rod is rubbed with wool, the two objects acquire a net charge of the same sign.
questions.explanation: Touching a neutral sphere with a positive object removes electrons, so the sphere becomes positive.

questions.questionText: A parallel plate capacitor is charged with a battery. The battery is then disconnected, and a dielectric material is inserted between the plates of the capacitor. Which of the following is correct about the effect of the dielectric?
options: The potential difference between the plates remains the same and the charge increases.
The charge on the plates decreases and the energy stored decreases.
The electric field between the plates and the energy stored decrease.
The capacitance remains the same and the electric field between the plates increases.
questions.explanation:
When the battery is disconnected, the charge on the capacitor remains constant.

 Inserting a dielectric increases the capacitance (C → κC), so the voltage V = Q/C decreases.

 As a result, the electric field E = V/d decreases and the energy stored U = ½ Q²/C also decreases.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the resistance of a conductor with a circular cross-section?
options: At a given temperature, the resistance of copper and silver wires of the same length and diameter is the same.
The resistance of the conductor increases as its length increases and its diameter decreases.
The resistance of the conductor increases as its length and diameter increases.
The resistance of the conductor decreases as it is heated.
questions.explanation:
The resistance of a conductor is given by R = ρL/A, where ρ is the resistivity, L is the length, and A is the cross-sectional area.

 For a circular cross-section, A ∝ diameter².

 Therefore, resistance increases with length and decreases with diameter.

 Heating generally increases resistance.

questions.questionText: A student wants to investigate Ohm's law using an ammeter (A) and a voltmeter (V) to measure current through and potential difference across a resistor (R). Moreover, she employs a rheostat to vary the potential difference across the resistor. Which of the following connections is the correct set up of the circuit to perform the experiment?
questions.explanation:
Ammeter must be in series to measure current, voltmeter must be in parallel across the resistor, and rheostat in series to vary current.

 Only option B satisfies all.

questions.questionText: Circular paths followed by two charges q1 and q2 moving with the same speed in a uniform magnetic field directed into the page (times) are shown in the figure below. If the two charges have the same mass, which of the following is correct about the sign and the magnitude of charges?
options: q1 is negative, q2 is positive and |q1| < |q2|.
q1 is negative, q2 is positive and |q1| > |q2|.
q1 is positive, q2 is negative and |q1| > |q2|.
q1 is positive, q2 is negative and |q1| < |q2|.
questions.explanation:
Using right-hand rule: in a magnetic field into the page, clockwise motion means positive charge and anticlockwise means negative.

 So q1 is positive and q2 is negative.

 Also, larger radius means smaller charge (r = mv / |q|B).

 Since q1 has larger radius, |q1| < |q2|.

questions.questionText: The primary coil of a transformer has 250 turns and its secondary coil consists of 1500 turns. If 220 V is applied to its primary coil, the voltage induced in the secondary coil and the ratio of current in the primary coil to the current in the secondary coil, respectively, are ______.
questions.explanation:
For an ideal transformer, Vₛ / Vₚ = Nₛ / Nₚ and Iₚ / Iₛ = Nₛ / Nₚ.

Here, Nₚ = 250, Nₛ = 1500, Vₚ = 220 V.

Vₛ = (Nₛ / Nₚ) × Vₚ = (1500 / 250) × 220 = 6 × 220 = 1320 V.

The current ratio Iₚ / Iₛ = Nₛ / Nₚ = 1500 / 250 = 6.

questions.questionText: A diode is an electronic component that ______.
options: is useful to convert a DC voltage to AC voltage.
allows electric current to pass through in one direction.
allows the flow of current when its p-type region is connected to the negative terminal of a cell.
allows current to pass through it either from cathode to anode or from anode to cathode.
questions.explanation:
A diode is a semiconductor device that acts as a one-way switch for current.

 It is primarily designed to allow current to flow easily in one direction (forward bias) and to block current flow in the opposite direction (reverse bias). 

This property makes it essential for rectification (converting AC to pulsing DC).

questions.questionText: Three forces, each having equal magnitudes of 10N, are applied to an object on a horizontal surface. A force F1 makes an angle of 30° above positive x-axis, F2 makes 30° above the negative x-axis, and the third force F3 is directed along the positive y-axis. The magnitude and direction of their resultant force are, respectively, ______.
A student throws a ball vertically upward with a speed of 20 m/s. The maximum height reached by the ball and its velocity 3.0 s after it was thrown are, respectively, ______.
questions.explanation:
The ball is thrown vertically upward with initial speed u = 20 m/s. Taking acceleration due to gravity g = 10 m/s² downward.

 The maximum height reached is given by h = u² / (2g) = (20²) / (2 × 10) = 400 / 20 = 20 m.

 The velocity after 3.0 s is given by v = u − gt = 20 − (10 × 3) = −10 m/s.

 The negative sign indicates downward direction.

 Hence, the maximum height is 20 m and the velocity after 3.0 s is 10 m/s downward.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements describes the difference between different types of friction?
options: For an object at rest on a horizontal surface, static friction increases with the increase of the applied force and reaches a maximum value just before sliding occurs.
Limiting friction is the minimum value of static friction that keeps an object stationary.
If there is a constant force applied to a stationary object on a horizontal surface, the static friction becomes equal to the limiting friction.
Limiting and kinetic frictions exist at the same time between two surfaces sliding over each other.
questions.explanation:
Static friction acts on an object at rest and adjusts itself to match the applied force until it reaches a maximum value called limiting friction, just before the object starts sliding. This behavior is correctly described in option 1.

 Option 2 is incorrect because limiting friction is the maximum, not the minimum, value of static friction. 

Option 3 is incorrect because static friction equals the applied force only up to the limiting value, not necessarily equal to it for every constant force.

 Option 4 is incorrect because limiting friction acts just before motion starts, while kinetic friction acts after sliding begins; they do not exist at the same time.

questions.questionText: The apparent weight of a 60 kg student standing inside a lift is
options: 600 N when the lift accelerates with acceleration equal to gravitational acceleration.
480 N when the lift accelerates upward with 2 m/s².
480 N when the lift accelerates downward with 2 m/s².
720 N when the lift is at rest.
questions.explanation:
The apparent weight of a person in a lift is the normal reaction N. For a mass m = 60 kg and g = 10 m/s²: 

(i) If the lift accelerates upward with acceleration a, N = m(g + a). 

(ii) If the lift accelerates downward with acceleration a, N = m(g − a). 

(iii) If the lift is at rest, N = mg. 

Now checking the options: For upward acceleration of 2 m/s², N = 60(10 + 2) = 720 N, not 480 N, so option 2 is incorrect. 

For downward acceleration of 2 m/s², N = 60(10 − 2) = 480 N, which matches option 3. 

When the lift is at rest, N = 60 × 10 = 600 N, not 720 N, so option 4 is incorrect. 

If the lift accelerates with acceleration equal to g, the apparent weight is either 0 (downward) or 1200 N (upward), not 600 N, so option 1 is incorrect.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements describe the use of energy resources?
options: Solar energy produced by photovoltaic cells is free of greenhouse gases and has a very low running cost.
Hydroelectric power generates a large amount of energy using small dams with little environmental impact and cheap initial cost of construction.
Geothermal energy is the most accessible, environmental friendly and inexpensive source of energy.
Wind energy, which is due to the pressure difference in space as the result of uneven sun heat, is a consistent and economical source of energy.
questions.explanation: Solar PV produces no greenhouse gases during use and has low running cost; others are incorrect due to environmental impact, accessibility, or inconsistency.

questions.questionText: A student wants to raise an object of mass m through a height h using an inclined plane that makes an angle θ above the horizontal. If l is the length of the inclined surface, which one of the following is correct about the actual mechanical advantage (AMA) and ideal mechanical advantage (IMA) of the inclined plane?
options: In the presence of friction, its AMA is 1/sinθ
In the absence of friction, AMA is sinθ and its IMA is cosθ.
questions.explanation:
For an inclined plane of length l and height h, sinθ = h / l.

 The ideal mechanical advantage (IMA) is defined as distance moved by effort divided by distance moved by load, so IMA = l / h = 1 / sinθ. 

In the absence of friction, the actual mechanical advantage (AMA) equals the IMA, hence AMA = 1 / sinθ.

 In the presence of friction, AMA is always less than IMA, so it cannot be equal to 1 / sinθ. 

Therefore, the correct statement is that neglecting friction, the AMA of the inclined plane is 1 / sinθ.

questions.questionText: According to the law of floatation, an object displaces a volume of fluid ______.
options: equal to the weight of undisplaced fluid.
questions.explanation:
According to the law of floatation, a floating object displaces a volume of fluid whose weight is equal to the weight of the object.

 This is because, for a body to float, the buoyant force (which equals the weight of the displaced fluid) must balance the weight of the object.

 Hence, the correct statement is that the displaced fluid has weight equal to the weight of the object.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements describes the unusual behavior of water?
options: The density of water at 0°C is less than its density at 4°C, since water molecules move further apart and form a second hydrogen bond with other water molecules.
As a temperature of water increases above 4°C, its density increases since water molecules move further apart to form a second hydrogen bond with other molecules.
At 0°C, water has larger density and smaller volume than its density and volume at 4°C.
As a temperature of water increases from 0°C to 4°C, its density increases since one molecule of water forms one hydrogen bond with another molecule.
questions.explanation:
Water exhibits an unusual behavior in that its density is maximum at 4°C. From 0°C to 4°C, as ice melts and water warms, its density increases (volume decreases) because the hydrogen-bonded structure of ice breaks slightly, allowing molecules to come closer. 

At 0°C, water has lower density and larger volume than at 4°C. This is correctly described in option 1, which states that at 0°C, water molecules are more spread out due to hydrogen bonding. 

Options 2 and 3 are incorrect because density does not increase above 4°C due to hydrogen bonding; option 4 incorrectly describes hydrogen bonding formation.

questions.questionText: A 40g of water at 50°C is poured into a well-insulated 30g of copper calorimeter at 20°C. The temperature of water at equilibrium becomes
questions.explanation:
Heat lost by water = heat gained by copper.

 mw*cw*(Twi - Tf) = mc*cc*(Tf - Tci). 

Substituting: 40*4.2*(50 - Tf) = 30*0.4*(Tf - 20) 

→ 168*(50 - Tf) = 12*(T_f - 20). 

Solving gives Tf ≈ 47.9°C.

questions.questionText: An FM radio signal is transmitted from a radio station at a frequency of 1.5 * 10⁸Hz. If the wavelength of the radio wave is 2.00 m, the speed of the FM signal is
questions.explanation:
The speed of a wave is given by v = f * λ.

 Here, f = 1.5 × 10⁸ Hz and λ = 2.00 m.

 So, v = 1.5 ×10⁸ * 2 = 3 × 10⁸ m/s. 

Hence, the speed of the FM signal is 3 ×10⁸ m/s

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about transformation of mechanical energy into other forms and the law of conservation of total energy?
options: Due to dissipative force, the mechanical energy of a wooden block sliding on a rough horizontal surface is not conserved.
Mechanical energy of a wooden block sliding on a rough horizontal surface is conserved.
Neglecting air resistance, an object moving vertically downward gains potential energy and loses an equal amount of kinetic energy.
Neglecting air resistance, an object moving vertically upward gains kinetic energy and loses an equal amount of gravitational potential energy.
questions.explanation:
Mechanical energy (ME) is the sum of kinetic and potential energy.

 It is not conserved when non-conservative (dissipative) forces like friction are present, as friction converts ME into internal energy (heat).

 The total energy of the system, however, remains conserved.

questions.questionText: A wheel rotating at angular speed of 20 rev/s is brought to rest after 40 rev under a constant angular acceleration. The angular acceleration of a point on the wheel is
questions.explanation:
Given: initial angular speed ω = 20 rev/s, final angular speed ωf = 0, angular displacement θ = 40 rev. 

Using equation ωf² = ω² + 2αθ, 

we have 0 = 20² + 2*α*40 

→ 0 = 400 + 80α 
→ α = -400/80 = -5 rev/s².

 The negative sign indicates angular deceleration.

questions.questionText: The parallel axis theorem states that if Icm is the moment of inertia of a body of mass M about an axis passing through its center of mass (CM), its moment of inertia about any axis is
options: perpendicular to and a displacement d from the axis through the cm is I = Icm + 1/2 Md².
parallel to and a displacement d from the axis through the cm is I = Icm + Md².
perpendicular to and a displacement d from the axis through the cm is I = Icm - Md².
parallel to and a displacement d from the axis through the cm is I = Icm  1/2 Md².
questions.explanation:
The parallel axis theorem states that the moment of inertia of a body about any axis parallel to an axis through its center of mass (CM) is given by I = Icm + Md²,

 where M is the mass of the body and d is the perpendicular distance between the axes.

 Hence, the correct option is the one describing a parallel axis and I = Icm + Md².

questions.questionText: Three forces of equal magnitude F are exerted at the center of a uniform beam of length L and negligible mass. The net torques on the beam about an axis parallel to the z-axis and passing through point A, B, and O, respectively, which one of the following expressions is correct?
questions.explanation: τ_net = r × Fnet = r × 0 = 0

questions.questionText: Tensile stress is the
options: parallel component of the applied force divided by the cross sectional area on an object.
ratio of change in length of an object to the original length.
perpendicular component of the applied force divided by the cross sectional area of an object.
ratio of original length to the change in length of the object.
questions.explanation:
Tensile stress is defined as the force applied perpendicular to the cross-sectional area of an object divided by that area.

 It measures how much internal resisting force per unit area develops when the object is subjected to stretching. 

Hence, it is the perpendicular component of the applied force divided by the cross-sectional area.

questions.questionText: A certain fluid has a density of 1080  kg/m³and is observed to rise to a height of 2.1cm in a 1.0mm diameter tube. If the contact angle between the wall and the surface is zero, the surface tension of the fluid is
questions.explanation:
Given: ρ = 1080 kg/m³, h = 2.1 cm = 0.021 m, r = 1.0 mm / 2 = 0.0005 m, g = 9.8 m/s², contact angle θ = 0°. 

Capillary rise formula: h = 2T cosθ / (ρ g r) → T = (h ρ g r) / (2 cosθ).

 Substituting: T = (0.021 * 1080 * 9.8 * 0.0005) / 2 ≈ 0.0557 ≈ 0.0567 N/m.

questions.questionText: A slab of thermal insulator has a cross-section of 0.1 m² , a length of 2 cm, and thermal conductivity of 0.1 J/(m.s °C).  If the temperature difference between the opposite faces of the insulator is 100°C , the amount of heat flowing through the slab in 24 h is
questions.explanation:
Given: A = 0.1 m², L = 0.02 m, k = 0.1 J/(m·s·°C), ΔT = 100°C, t = 24 h = 86400 s.

 Using Fourier's law: Q = k*A*ΔT*t / L. Step 1: k*A*ΔT = 0.1*0.1*100 = 1.

 Step 2: Multiply by time: 1*86400 = 86400 J. 

Step 3: Divide by thickness: Q = 86400 / 0.02 = 4.32 × 10⁶ J. 

Hence, the heat flowing through the slab in 24 h is 4.32 × 10⁶ J

questions.questionText: A 100 J of work is done on a system and 418.6 J of heat is extracted from it. According to the first law of thermodynamics, the change in the internal energy of the system is
questions.explanation:
The first law of thermodynamics states: ΔU = Q - W, where ΔU is the change in internal energy, Q is heat added to the system, W is work done by the system. 

Here, Q = -418.6 J (heat extracted from the system), W = 100 J (work done on the system is positive for work done on system? careful). 

Using the sign convention where work done on the system is positive: ΔU = Q + W = -418.6 + 100 = -318.6 J. 

Hence, the internal energy decreases by 318.6 J.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements describe the difference between reversible and irreversible processes?
options: In an irreversible process, a system can move from one thermodynamic state to another and back to its initial state; whereas a system in a reversible process cannot move back to its initial state.
system undergoing a reversible process is always close to thermodynamic equilibrium; whereas a system undergoing irreversible process is not in thermal equilibrium.
Ice at 0°C placed in a metallic can at 40°C undergoes a reversible process; whereas ice at 0°C placed in a metal can at 0°C undergoes an irreversible process.
process is reversible if its entropy increases, but irreversible if its entropy is constant.
questions.explanation:
A reversible process is one in which the system remains infinitesimally close to thermodynamic equilibrium at all times, allowing it to be reversed without leaving any change in the surroundings.

 In contrast, an irreversible process is far from equilibrium and cannot be reversed without leaving changes in the surroundings.

 Therefore, the correct statement is: 'A system undergoing a reversible process is always close to thermodynamic equilibrium; whereas a system undergoing an irreversible process is not in thermal equilibrium.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about resonance in an oscillating object?
options: At resonance, the driving frequency is equal to the natural frequency and the amplitude becomes maximum.
Damping increases the amplitude and natural frequency of the oscillator.
Resonance occurs when the frequency of a periodic driving force is greater than the natural frequency of the oscillator.
Resonance occurs when the oscillator is subject to a constant driving force.
questions.explanation:
Resonance in an oscillating system occurs when the frequency of the external periodic driving force matches the natural frequency of the system.

 At this point, the amplitude of oscillation becomes maximum. 

Damping actually reduces the amplitude and slightly lowers the natural frequency.

 Therefore, the correct statement is: 'At resonance, the driving frequency is equal to the natural frequency and the amplitude becomes maximum.

questions.questionText: Moment of inertia depends on:
questions.explanation: I = Σ m r² depends on how mass is distributed about rotation axis.

questions.questionText: Among the following analog circuits, consisting of two switches A and B, a lamp Y, and voltage source, which one functions as a NAND gate?
options: Parallel switches in series with lamp Y (OR gate)
Series switches in series with lamp Y (AND gate)
Series switches A and B connected in parallel across lamp Y
Parallel switches A and B connected in parallel across lamp Y (NOR gate)
questions.explanation:
A NAND gate produces a LOW output only when both inputs are HIGH.

In the given circuit, when both switches A and B are closed, the parallel path bypasses the lamp, causing the lamp to turn off.

For all other combinations, the lamp remains on.

Thus, the circuit behaves according to the NAND truth table.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the properties of waves?
options: When two waves interfere destructively, the amplitude of the resultant wave is greater than the amplitude of each wave.
Diffraction of a wave through a narrow gap is more observable than through a wider gap.
When a wave is reflected, its speed and wavelength are changed.
When a wave is refracted, its speed and wavelength remain the same.
questions.explanation:
* **Option A is incorrect:** Destructive interference results in a smaller amplitude, not a greater one.
* **Option B is correct:** Diffraction is the spreading of waves. It is most noticeable when the size of the aperture (gap) is comparable to or smaller than the wavelength of the wave. A narrow gap maximizes the observable diffraction effect.
* **Option C is incorrect:** Reflection occurs in the same medium, so the speed and wavelength remain unchanged.
* **Option D is incorrect:** Refraction (bending) occurs when a wave enters a new medium, which causes its **speed** and **wavelength** to change, while its frequency remains constant.

questions.questionText: Consider a particle performing a circular motion around a circle of radius r, with an angular velocity omega, and the particle's projection on the horizontal diameter of the circle (between points $Q$ and R) as shown in the figure below. Which one of the following statements is correct about the motion of the particle and its projection on QR?
options: The projection of the particle on QR swings between points Q and R with constant speed.
The circular motion of the particle can be taken as a simple harmonic motion.
The projection of the particle on QR demonstrates simple harmonic motion.
The projection of the particle on QR demonstrates motion with constant acceleration.
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which of the following concepts of physics are the primary focus points in mechanical engineering?
options: Geometric optics, Electrostatics, Thermodynamics, and Stress
Nuclear physics, Geometric optics, Dynamics, and Force
Molecular physics, Dynamics, Nuclear physics, and Force
questions.explanation:
Mechanical engineering is primarily concerned with the design, analysis, manufacturing, and maintenance of mechanical systems. The core physics concepts central to this field include:
* **Dynamics:** The study of motion and its causes (forces and torques), which is crucial for analyzing machine performance.
* **Thermodynamics:** The study of heat, work, temperature, and energy, essential for engines, HVAC systems, and power generation.
* **Force (and Statics):** The foundational concepts of push/pull and equilibrium, necessary for structural integrity and machine design.
* **Stress (and Material Science):** The analysis of internal forces within materials, critical for ensuring parts don't fail under load.

Therefore, **Dynamics, Thermodynamics, Force, and Stress** are the most relevant concepts. Geometric optics, electrostatics, and nuclear/molecular physics are not primary focus points.

questions.questionText: Given vector A⃗ having magnitude A, a unit vector, Ûₐ, in the direction of A⃗  is defines as
questions.explanation:
A unit vector in the direction of a given vector is defined as the vector itself divided by its magnitude:

 u_A = A / A.

questions.questionText: Which electromagnetic radiation is commonly used in thermal imaging and night-vision systems because objects emit it according to their temperature?
questions.explanation:
Objects emit thermal radiation, much of which lies in the infrared region for ordinary temperatures.

Infrared detectors can therefore reveal temperature differences and are useful in thermal imaging and night vision.

questions.questionText: A convex lens has focal length 20 cm. An object is placed 30 cm from the lens. Where is the image formed?
questions.explanation:
Using the lens equation 1/f = 1/v - 1/u with u = -30 cm and f = 20 cm,

1/v = 1/20 - 1/30 = 1/60.

Therefore, v = 60 cm.

The real image forms 60 cm from the lens.

questions.questionText: 50. The angular speed of a disk rotating about its axis increases by $2000 \text{ rad/s}$ in a time interval of $3.0 \text{ s}$. If the moment of inertia of the disk is $0.6 \text{ kg} \text{ m}^2$, what is the average torque on the disk?
questions.explanation:
The average torque ($\tau$) is given by the relationship $\tau = I \alpha$, where $I$ is the moment of inertia and $\alpha$ is the average angular acceleration.

1.  **Calculate Angular Acceleration ($\alpha$):** 
$$\alpha = \frac{\Delta\omega}{\Delta t} = \frac{2000 \text{ rad/s}}{3.0 \text{ s}} = \frac{2000}{3} \text{ rad/s}^2$$

2.  **Calculate Average Torque ($\tau$):**
$$\tau = I \alpha = (0.6 \text{ kg} \text{ m}^2) \left( \frac{2000}{3} \text{ rad/s}^2 \right) = \left( \frac{0.6}{3} \right) \times 2000$$
$$\tau = 0.2 \times 2000 = 400 \text{ Nm}$$

questions.questionText:
The North pole of a bar magnet is moving away from a circular wire lying on the top of a horizontal table as shown in the figure below.

According to Lenz's law, the direction of the induced current in the wire when viewed from the magnetic side is
questions.explanation:
According to Lenz's law, the induced current will oppose the change in magnetic flux.

 Since the North pole is moving away, the loop creates a South pole on top to attract it back.

 Looking down at a South pole, the direction of the current flows clockwise.

questions.questionText: A substance of mass 2 kg receives 18,000 J of heat and its temperature rises by 30°C. What is its specific heat capacity?
questions.explanation:
Using Q = mcΔT,

c = Q/(mΔT) = 18,000/(2 × 30) = 300 J/kg·°C.

Therefore, the specific heat capacity is 300 J/kg·°C.

questions.questionText: An object moving in one dimension with constant acceleration, $a$, travels through a displacement $s$ in a time interval $t$. If its velocity at the initial time $t=0$ is $v_0$ and its velocity at a later time $t$ is $v$, which of the following is a correct relation between the given quantities?
questions.explanation: For motion with **constant acceleration**, the displacement ($s$) is the product of the average velocity and the time interval ($t$). The average velocity is $\frac{v_0 + v}{2}$. Therefore, the correct relation is $s = \text{Average velocity} \times t = \frac{(v_0 + v)}{2}t$. (Note: Using $v_i$ for $v_0$ and $v_f$ for $v$). Option C uses $v_f$ and $v_i$ correctly.

questions.questionText: 23. About an axis of rotation perpendicular to a plane of a couple, the forces in a couple produce
questions.explanation:
A couple consists of two equal and opposite forces that do not share the same line of action.

 Although the net force is zero, each force creates a torque (turning effect) around the center of mass.

questions.questionText: A radioactive sample initially contains 8000 nuclei. If its half-life is 5 hours, approximately how many nuclei remain after 15 hours?
questions.explanation:
Fifteen hours corresponds to three half-lives.

After one half-life: 4000 nuclei remain.

After two: 2000 remain.

After three: 1000 remain.

Therefore, 1000 nuclei remain.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is **correct about real and virtual images**?
options: **Real images can be displayed on a screen unlike the virtual ones**.
Virtual images can be displayed on a screen unlike the real ones.
Virtual images can be magnified but real images cannot.
Real images can be magnified but virtual images cannot.
questions.explanation: A **real image** is formed where light rays actually converge; thus, it can be projected onto a screen. A **virtual image** is formed where light rays appear to diverge from a point but do not actually converge; it cannot be projected onto a screen (e.g., the image seen in a plane mirror). Both real and virtual images can be magnified or demagnified depending on the optical system (lens or mirror) used.

questions.questionText: A force of 50 N acts on an object through a displacement of 12 m at an angle of 60° to the displacement. How much work is done by the force?
questions.explanation:
Work is W = Fdcosθ.

Therefore, W = 50(12)cos60° = 600(0.5) = 300 J.

questions.questionText: A fluid travelling over a body's surface exerts less pressure than if the fluid was static. This is a statement of:
questions.explanation:
Bernoulli's principle states that for a flowing fluid, an increase in the speed of the fluid occurs simultaneously with a decrease in pressure. 

Therefore, a fluid moving over a surface exerts less pressure than the same fluid at rest.

questions.questionText: 32. Which one of the following statements is correct about the resistance of a conducting wire? The resistance of the wire is
options: directly proportional to the square of its length.
directly proportional to the square of its cross-sectional area.
inversely proportional to its cross-sectional area.
questions.explanation:
The resistance (R) of a conductor is given by the formula R = pL/A, where rho is resistivity, L is length, and A is the cross-sectional area.

 The formula shows that resistance is inversely proportional to the cross-sectional area  and

 directly proportional to the length.

questions.questionText: A uniform beam is 6 m long and weighs 120 N. It is supported at both ends. A 180 N load is placed 2 m from the left support. What is the reaction force at the right support?
questions.explanation:
Take moments about the left support.

R_B(6) = 120(3) + 180(2).

Thus, 6R_B = 360 + 360 = 720.

Therefore, R_B = 120 N.

questions.questionText: 21. When a force F is applied to a wire of length L fixed at one end, the wire extends by $x$. The tensile strain of the wire is
options: the length L divided by the extension $x$.
the extension $x$ divided by the length L.
the product of the force F and the extension $x$.
the applied force F divided by the extension.
questions.explanation:
Tensile **strain** ($epsilon$) is defined as the ratio of the change in length ($Delta L$) to the original length ($L_0$). In this case, the extension is $\Delta L = x$ and the original length is $L_0 = L$:
$$\text{Strain} = \epsilon = \frac{\Delta L}{L_0} = \frac{x}{L}$$

questions.questionText: The critical angle for a glass-air boundary is approximately 42°. What happens when a ray inside the glass strikes the boundary at an angle of 50° to the normal?
options: It passes normally into the air.
It bends toward the normal in the air.
questions.explanation:
Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from a denser medium to a less dense medium and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle.

Since 50° > 42°, total internal reflection occurs.

questions.questionText: How much heat is required to raise 0.50 kg of water from 25°C to 85°C? Take the specific heat capacity of water as 4200 J/kg·°C.
questions.explanation:
The temperature change is 60°C.

Q = mcΔT = 0.50(4200)(60) = 126,000 J.

questions.questionText: A sound wave has frequency 500 Hz and wavelength 0.68 m. What is its speed?
questions.explanation:
Wave speed is v = fλ.

Therefore, v = 500(0.68) = 340 m/s.

questions.questionText: 60. A substance with a mass of $2 \text{ kg}$ has a volume of $2.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3$. What is the relative density of the substance?
questions.explanation:
Relative density ($RD$) is the ratio of the density of the substance ($\rho_{sub}$) to the density of water ($\rho_{water} = 1000 \text{ kg/m}^3$).

1.  **Calculate the Density of the Substance ($\rho_{sub}$):**
$$\rho_{sub} = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Volume}} = \frac{2 \text{ kg}}{2.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3} = 800 \text{ kg/m}^3$$

2.  **Calculate Relative Density:**
$$RD = \frac{\rho_{sub}}{\rho_{water}} = \frac{800 \text{ kg/m}^3}{1000 \text{ kg/m}^3} = 0.8$$

questions.questionText: Two plane mirrors inclined at an angle of 72° to each other. How many images are formed when an object is placed between them?
questions.explanation:
For two plane mirrors inclined at an angle θ, when 360°/θ is an integer, the number of images is n = 360°/θ - 1.

Here, θ = 72°, so 360°/72° = 5.

Therefore, n = 5 - 1 = 4 images.

questions.questionText: Water flows through a horizontal pipe at 4.0 m/s where its pressure is 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa. If the pipe narrows so that the water speed becomes 10.0 m/s, what is the pressure in the narrower section? Take the density of water as 1000 kg/m³.
questions.explanation:
For horizontal flow, Bernoulli's equation gives P₁ + ½ρv₁² = P₂ + ½ρv₂².

Thus, P₂ = P₁ + ½ρ(v₁² - v₂²).

P₂ = 1.8 × 10⁵ + 500(16 - 100) =
 1.38 × 10⁵ Pa.

Therefore, the pressure decreases as the fluid speed increases.

questions.questionText: A square metal plate of coefficient of linear expansion $\alpha$, has a surface area $A_0$ at a temperature $T_0$. If the temperature is raised by an amount $\Delta T$, then the plate surface area is changed to $A$, which is expressed as
questions.explanation:
The change in area due to thermal expansion is called **area expansion** (or superficial expansion). The area expansion coefficient ($\beta$) is approximately twice the linear expansion coefficient ($\alpha$), i.e., $\beta \approx 2\alpha$.

The formula for the new area ($A$) is given by:
$$A = A_0 (1 + \beta \Delta T)$$
Substituting $\beta = 2\alpha$:
$$A = A_0 (1 + 2\alpha \Delta T)$$

*Note: Options B and C are identical and incorrect, and Option D is for volume expansion ($\gamma \approx 3\alpha$).*

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about critical and boiling points?
options: The critical point of a substance is constant, while its boiling point is dependent on the surrounding pressure.
The critical point is dependent both on temperature and pressure, while boiling point is independent of the surrounding pressure.
At the boiling point a single gaseous phase exists, while at the critical point both the liquid and gas phases coexist.
The boiling point of a substance is constant independent of pressure, while its critical point is dependent on the surrounding temperature.
questions.explanation:
The critical point is a characteristic point of a substance defined by a particular critical temperature and critical pressure.

Above the critical temperature, a gas cannot be liquefied simply by increasing pressure.

The boiling point, however, depends on the surrounding pressure and changes when the external pressure changes.

questions.questionText:
The figure shown below illustrates how the mass attached to a spring oscillates along a horizontal frictionless surface between points A and B.

How can one explain the mechanical energy of the mass-spring system for this figure? Its mechanical energy is equal to its
options: elastic potential energy when the mass is at position O.
kinetic energy when the mass is at position B.
kinetic energy when the mass is at position A.
kinetic energy when the mass is at position O.
questions.explanation:
At the equilibrium position O, the stretch/compression of the spring is zero, so elastic potential energy is zero and all mechanical energy is in the form of maximum kinetic energy.

 At turning points A and B, kinetic energy is zero and all energy is elastic potential energy.

questions.questionText: A 2 kg object is attached to a string and moves in a vertical circle. At the top of the circle, its speed is 5 m/s and the radius is 1.0 m. What is the minimum tension required at the top? Take g = 10 m/s².
questions.explanation:
At the top, both tension and weight point toward the center.

T + mg = mv²/r.

Thus, T = mv²/r - mg = 2(25) - 20 = 30 N.

questions.questionText: A wave has a period of 0.020 s and travels at 300 m/s. What is its wavelength?
questions.explanation:
Frequency is f = 1/T = 50 Hz.

Using v = fλ,

λ = v/f = 300/50 = 6 m.

questions.questionText: The graph given below shows the velocity of a man travelling on a motorcycle as a function of time. Which one of the following statements is correct about the velocity-time graph?
options: The displacement during the time interval from t = 6s to t = 14s is equal to the area of region II minus the area of region III.
The displacement during the time interval from t = 0s to t = 6s is equal to the area under the velocity-time graph in the given interval.
The acceleration during the time interval from t = 6s to t = 10s is equal to the gradient of the curve in the given interval and it is negative.
The acceleration in the first 6s is equal to the gradient of the curve in the given interval and it is positive.
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: A 5 Ω resistor carries a current of 3 A. What electrical power is dissipated by the resistor?
questions.explanation:
Electrical power can be calculated using P = I²R.

P = 3²(5) = 45 W.

questions.questionText: A $2 \text{ kg}$ object accelerates with $1.5 \text{ m/s}^2$ to the right on a horizontal frictionless surface under the action of two horizontal forces, $F_1$ and $F_2$, as shown in the figure below. What should be the magnitude of $F_1$?
questions.explanation:
This problem is solved using **Newton's Second Law of Motion**: $\text{Net Force} = \text{mass} \times \text{acceleration}$ ($F_{net} = ma$).
1. **Identify the variables:** 
   * Mass, $m = 2 \text{ kg}$
   * Acceleration, $a = 1.5 \text{ m/s}^2$ (to the right, positive direction)
   * Force $F_2 = 1 \text{ N}$ (to the left, negative direction)
   * Force $F_1 = ?$ (to the right, positive direction)
2. **Write the equation for the net force (sum of forces):**
   $F_{net} = F_1 - F_2$ (Assuming right is positive)
3. **Substitute into Newton's Second Law:**
   $F_1 - F_2 = m \times a$
4. **Solve for $F_1$:**
   $F_1 - 1 \text{ N} = (2 \text{ kg}) \times (1.5 \text{ m/s}^2)$
   $F_1 - 1 \text{ N} = 3 \text{ N}$
   $F_1 = 3 \text{ N} + 1 \text{ N}$
   $F_1 = 4 \text{ N}$

questions.questionText: A parallel-plate capacitor is charged to voltage V and then disconnected from the battery. A dielectric material with dielectric constant 4 is inserted completely between its plates. What happens to its stored energy?
questions.explanation:
After the battery is disconnected, charge remains constant.

The energy is U = Q²/(2C).

Insertion of a dielectric increases capacitance by a factor of 4, so the energy decreases by a factor of 4.

Thus, the new energy is one-fourth of the original.

questions.questionText: A 2 kg object moving at 6 m/s collides with a stationary 4 kg object. If they stick together after collision, what is their common velocity?
questions.explanation:
Momentum is conserved in the absence of external impulse.

Initial momentum = 2(6) + 4(0) = 12 kg·m/s.

The combined mass is 6 kg.

Therefore, v = 12/6 = 2 m/s.

questions.questionText: An electromagnetic wave has a frequency of 6.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz. Taking the speed of light as 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s, what is its wavelength?
questions.explanation:
The wave equation is c = fλ.

Therefore, λ = c/f = (3.0 × 10⁸)/(6.0 × 10¹⁴) = 5.0 × 10⁻⁷ m.

questions.questionText: The difference between conventional X-ray and CT-scan is that in the case of X-ray the machine that sends X-rays through the patient's body is
options: stationary, whereas in CT-scan a rotating X-ray machine is used.
rotating in the opposite direction of the detector which are stationary in the case of CT-scan.
rotating, whereas in CT-scan a stationary X-ray machine is used.
stationary but the patient is moving, unlike in case of CT scan.
questions.explanation:
In conventional X-ray imaging, the X-ray source remains essentially stationary and produces a two-dimensional projection image.

In a CT scan, the X-ray source and detectors rotate around the patient to collect many projections from different angles.

These measurements are then used to construct cross-sectional images.

questions.questionText: A planet has an orbital radius nine times that of Earth. Assuming both planets orbit the Sun and Kepler's third law applies, approximately how many Earth years does the planet take to complete one orbit?
questions.explanation:
Kepler's third law gives T² ∝ R³.

Therefore, (T/T_E)² = 9³ = 729.

Taking the square root gives T/T_E = 27.

Thus, the planet requires approximately 27 Earth years for one orbit.

questions.questionText: A metal wire has a length of 2.0 m and cross-sectional area 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ m². If a force of 100 N produces an extension of 1.0 mm, what is the Young's modulus of the material?
questions.explanation:
Young's modulus is Y = FL/(AΔL).

Substituting F = 100 N, L = 2 m, A = 10⁻⁶ m² and ΔL = 10⁻³ m gives Y = 2 × 10¹¹ Pa.

questions.questionText: A 5 kg object is acted upon by two perpendicular forces of 12 N and 16 N. What is the magnitude of its acceleration?
questions.explanation:
The resultant force is √(12² + 16²) = 20 N.

Using Newton's second law, a = F/m = 20/5 = 4 m/s².

questions.questionText: Which one of the following phenomena occurs during change of phases of a matter? During a phase change from
options: gas to liquid, heat energy is absorbed by a substance while its temperature remains constant.
solid to liquid, heat energy is released from a substance while its temperature remains constant.
liquid to solid, heat energy is released from a substance while its temperature changes uniformly.
liquid to gas, heat energy is absorbed by a substance while its temperature remains constant.
questions.explanation: Phase changes occur at a constant temperature. During a phase change from **liquid to gas** (boiling/vaporization), heat energy is **absorbed** by the substance (this absorbed heat is called the latent heat of vaporization), and its temperature **remains constant** until all the liquid has turned into gas. Similarly, during gas to liquid (condensation), heat is released; during solid to liquid (melting), heat is absorbed; and during liquid to solid (freezing), heat is released. The temperature remains constant in all these processes, which is why options A and B are incorrect in terms of absorbed/released heat, and option C is incorrect because the temperature remains constant, not changes uniformly.

questions.questionText: An object dropped into a sea sinks to a depth of $100\ \text{m}$. Which of the following is correct about the pressure the object experiences? (Assume the density of seawater is $1050\ \text{kg/m}^3$ and the air above the sea exerts a pressure of $P_{\text{atmospheric}} = 1.01 \times 10^5\ \text{Pa}$, $g = 10\ \text{m/s}^2$)
options: The gauge pressure exerted on it is $P_{\text{gauge}} = 1.01 \times 10^5\ \text{Pa}$.
The absolute pressure exerted on it is $P_{\text{absolute}} = 0.30 \times 10^5\ \text{Pa}$.
The absolute pressure exerted on it is $P_{\text{absolute}} = 1.13 \times 10^6\ \text{Pa}$.
The gauge pressure exerted on it is $P_{\text{gauge}} = 1.03 \times 10^6\ \text{Pa}$.
questions.explanation:
1.  **Calculate Gauge Pressure ($P_{\text{gauge}}$):**
    The gauge pressure is the pressure due to the column of fluid (seawater) only. It is calculated using the formula $P_{\text{gauge}} = \rho g h$.
    * $\rho = 1050\ \text{kg/m}^3$
    * $g = 10\ \text{m/s}^2$
    * $h = 100\ \text{m}$
    $$P_{\text{gauge}} = (1050\ \text{kg/m}^3)(10\ \text{m/s}^2)(100\ \text{m}) = 1,050,000\ \text{Pa}$$ 
    $$P_{\text{gauge}} = 1.05 \times 10^6\ \text{Pa}$$ (Option D, $1.03 \times 10^6\ \text{Pa}$, is close but not exact).

2.  **Calculate Absolute Pressure ($P_{\text{absolute}}$):**
    The absolute pressure is the sum of the gauge pressure and the atmospheric pressure ($P_{\text{atmospheric}}$) exerted on the surface.
    $$P_{\text{absolute}} = P_{\text{atmospheric}} + P_{\text{gauge}}$$
    * $P_{\text{atmospheric}} = 1.01 \times 10^5\ \text{Pa} = 0.101 \times 10^6\ \text{Pa}$
    * $P_{\text{gauge}} = 1.05 \times 10^6\ \text{Pa}$
    $$P_{\text{absolute}} = (0.101 \times 10^6\ \text{Pa}) + (1.05 \times 10^6\ \text{Pa}) = 1.151 \times 10^6\ \text{Pa}$$

3.  **Compare with Options:**
    * $P_{\text{absolute}} = 1.151 \times 10^6\ \text{Pa}$ is closest to Option C: $1.13 \times 10^6\ \text{Pa}$. The slight discrepancy may be due to using a rounded value of $g$ or $\rho$ in the problem's source, but $1.13 \times 10^6\ \text{Pa}$ is the correct choice among the options. (Note: Option A incorrectly states gauge pressure is $1.01 \times 10^5\ \text{Pa}$, which is the atmospheric pressure.)

questions.questionText: A 30kg rigid body has a moment of inertia 45 kgm² about its center of mass. What is the moment of inertia when it rotates through an axis 2m away and parallel to the axis through the center of mass?
questions.explanation:
Using the parallel axis theorem: I = I_cm + Md²

Where:-  I_cm = 45 kg·m² (moment of inertia about center of mass)

- M = 30 kg (mass of the body)

- d = 2 m (distance between axes)

I = 45 + 30*(2)² = 45 + 30*4 = 45 + 120 = 165 kg·m²

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the new axis is 165 kg·m².

questions.questionText:
A straight conductor carrying a current I, which flows upward, is placed in uniform magnetic field B directed into the page, as shown in the figure below.

What will happen to the conductor?
options: It will be pushed to the right.
It will be pushed out of the page.
It will be pushed into the page.
It will be pushed to the left.
questions.explanation:
Using the right-hand rule for magnetic force (F = I L × B): 

-> point your fingers upward in the direction of the current (I),

-> curl them inward into the page in the direction of the magnetic field (B),

-> and your thumb points to the right, indicating the direction of the force pushing the conductor.

questions.questionText: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field with velocity perpendicular to the field. If its speed is doubled while the charge, mass and field remain unchanged, what happens to the radius of its circular path?
options: It becomes four times as large.
questions.explanation:
For perpendicular motion in a magnetic field, r = mv/(|q|B).

Therefore, the radius is directly proportional to speed.

Doubling the speed doubles the radius.

questions.questionText: Which electromagnetic radiation has a higher frequency than visible violet light?
questions.explanation:
In the electromagnetic spectrum, ultraviolet radiation has higher frequency and shorter wavelength than visible violet light.

Therefore, ultraviolet radiation has the higher frequency.

questions.questionText: A current-carrying wire carries current in the positive z-direction. At a point located on the positive x-axis, the magnetic field produced by the wire points in which direction?
questions.explanation:
The magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire forms circular paths.

Using the right-hand rule, point the thumb in the positive z-direction. At a point on the positive x-axis, the curled fingers point in the positive y-direction.

questions.questionText: A ray of light passes from glass of refractive index 1.50 into air. If the angle of incidence inside the glass is 40°, what is the approximate angle of refraction?
questions.explanation:
Snell's law gives n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂.

Thus, sinθ₂ = 1.50sin40° ≈ 1.50(0.643) = 0.965.

Therefore, θ₂ ≈ 75°.

questions.questionText: Two vectors have magnitudes 8 N and 15 N and are perpendicular to each other. What is the magnitude of their resultant?
questions.explanation:
For perpendicular vectors, the resultant magnitude is R = √(A² + B²).

R = √(8² + 15²) = √289 = 17 N.
